meta.source: CBDT official concordance table + Income Tax Act 2025 + TaxGuru comparative study
meta.disclaimer: Mappings are sourced from official CBDT publications. Plain-English summaries are for guidance only. Always verify with a qualified CA before acting on any mapping.

terminology.note: Direct replacement. Both refer to April 1 to March 31 period.
AY was the year following PY. Under new Act, Tax Year covers both concepts. Context-sensitive — flag for manual review.
In tax context only — flag for review as FY may still be used in non-tax contexts.
Term unchanged. Provisions moved to Section 404.

sections.plain_english_summary: Definitions retained but 'Previous Year' and 'Assessment Year' removed. Replaced by single 'Tax Year' concept. All references in documents to AY or PY should be reviewed.
The concept of 'Previous Year' is abolished. The new Act uses a single 'Tax Year' running April 1 to March 31. Documents using 'PY 2025-26' should now say 'Tax Year 2026-27'.
LTA exemption moved from Section 10(5) to Schedule III. The exemption rules and conditions remain unchanged — only the location in the Act changed. Payroll systems should update section reference.
Gratuity exemption moved to Schedule III. Exemption limit of ₹20 lakh for non-government employees unchanged. Payroll teams should update their section reference in offer letters and policies.
Commuted pension exemption moved into the deductions table under Section 19. Rules identical — government employees get full exemption; others get 1/3rd if gratuity received, else 1/2.
Leave encashment exemption moved into Section 19 deduction table. ₹25 lakh limit for non-government employees unchanged. Update HR policy documents to reference new section.

sections.new_ref: Schedule III (Table, Entry 11) read with Rule 279
sections.limit_changed_note: HRA exemption calculation unchanged but Hyderabad, Pune, Ahmedabad and Bengaluru now added to metro list qualifying for 50% salary exemption (up from 40%). Effective from Tax Year 2026-27.
sections.plain_english_summary: HRA exemption moved to Schedule III. Big change: Hyderabad, Pune, Ahmedabad, Bengaluru now get 50% metro rate like Delhi/Mumbai/Chennai/Kolkata (was 40% before). Check and update all HRA declarations immediately.
Section number unchanged. Salary remains taxable on due or receipt basis, whichever is earlier. No substantive change.

sections.old_title: Deductions from salary (Standard deduction, Entertainment allowance, Professional tax)
sections.limit_changed_note: Standard deduction increased from ₹50,000 to ₹75,000 under the new tax regime.
sections.plain_english_summary: Old Section 16 is now Section 19. Standard deduction raised to ₹75,000 (from ₹50,000) for those under the new regime. All payroll software must update both the section reference and the deduction amount.

sections.old_title: Income from House Property — charging section
sections.new_title: Income from House Property — charging section
sections.plain_english_summary: Section number unchanged for the charging section. House property income rules essentially unchanged. No action needed beyond noting the new Act applies from Tax Year 2026-27.
Moved to Section 21 (was 23). Annual value rules and municipal value / fair rent / standard rent hierarchy unchanged.
Moved to Section 22 (was 24). Standard deduction of 30% and interest on home loan deduction rules unchanged. ₹2 lakh cap on interest for self-occupied property continues.

sections.old_title: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession — charging section
sections.new_title: Income under head Profits and Gains of Business or Profession
sections.plain_english_summary: The business income charging section moved from 28 to 26. All income heads that were taxable under 28 remain taxable. No substantive change.
Depreciation moved to Section 33. Rates under Schedule II remain unchanged. WDV method and straight-line method rules intact. Update any internal depreciation policy documents.
The catch-all business expense deduction moved to Section 42. 'Wholly and exclusively for business' test unchanged. No impact on what is deductible.

sections.limit_changed_note: Tax audit threshold for IT and IT-enabled services companies raised from ₹300 crore to ₹2,000 crore under safe harbour provisions.
sections.plain_english_summary: Tax audit provisions moved to Section 58. Big change for IT companies: safe harbour threshold raised to ₹2,000 crore (from ₹300 crore). All tax audit engagement letters should reference Section 58 from Tax Year 2026-27.
Presumptive taxation for small businesses moved to Section 59. ₹3 crore turnover threshold and 8%/6% profit rates unchanged. Eligible businesses include trading, manufacturing, and most services.
Presumptive taxation for professionals (doctors, lawyers, CAs, architects etc.) moved to Section 60. ₹75 lakh gross receipts threshold and 50% profit rate unchanged.
Capital gains charging section moved to 67. All transfer of capital assets remains taxable. Short-term / long-term distinction based on holding period unchanged.
Capital gains computation rules moved to Section 70. Full value of consideration minus cost of acquisition minus improvement costs formula unchanged. Indexation rules continue for applicable assets.

sections.old_title: Exemption on sale of residential house
sections.new_title: Exemption on transfer of residential property
sections.plain_english_summary: Section 54 exemption (buy another house to save LTCG) moved to Section 81. 2-year purchase / 3-year construction window unchanged. ₹10 crore cap on exemption remains. Update any client advisory documents.

sections.new_title: Exemption on investment in specified bonds
sections.plain_english_summary: Bond investment exemption (NHAI/REC bonds) moved to Section 85. ₹50 lakh cap per year and 6-month reinvestment window unchanged. Lock-in of 5 years continues.

sections.old_title: Income from Other Sources — gifts etc.
sections.plain_english_summary: Other sources provisions moved to Section 92. ₹50,000 gift threshold above which gifts from non-relatives are taxable remains unchanged.

sections.new_title: Set-off of losses within same head
sections.plain_english_summary: Loss set-off rules moved to Section 108. Intra-head and inter-head set-off rules unchanged. Business losses can still be set off against other heads (except salary). Update loss computation worksheets.

sections.new_title: Carry forward and set-off of business losses
sections.plain_english_summary: Business loss carry-forward moved to Section 110. 8-year carry-forward period unchanged. Same-business continuity requirement remains for closely held companies.

sections.old_title: Deductions — Life insurance, PPF, ELSS etc.
sections.plain_english_summary: The popular ₹1.5 lakh deduction for LIC, PPF, ELSS, home loan principal etc. is now Section 123 read with Schedule XV. The ₹1.5 lakh limit is unchanged. Applies only under old tax regime — not available under new default regime.

sections.limit_changed_note: Senior citizen deduction limit raised from ₹50,000 to ₹1,00,000.
sections.plain_english_summary: Health insurance deduction moved to Section 126. Major change: senior citizens can now claim up to ₹1 lakh (was ₹50,000). Self + family limit of ₹25,000 unchanged. Only available under old tax regime.

sections.new_title: Deduction for interest on education loan
sections.plain_english_summary: Education loan interest deduction moved to Section 127. 8-year deduction period and full interest deduction (no cap) unchanged. Available for higher education loans.
Donation deduction moved to Section 130. 50%/100% deduction categories based on institution type unchanged. 10% of adjusted gross income cap unchanged. Update donation receipts format.
Section 80GG (rent deduction for those not getting HRA) moved to Section 131. ₹5,000/month cap unchanged. Still only for old tax regime filers.

sections.new_title: Deduction for interest on savings deposits
sections.plain_english_summary: Savings account interest deduction (₹10,000) moved to Section 146. Only for individuals and HUF, only on savings account interest (not FD). Unchanged substantively.

sections.limit_changed_note: Senior citizen interest deduction (FD + savings account) raised from ₹50,000 to ₹1,00,000.
sections.plain_english_summary: Senior citizen interest deduction moved to Section 147 with a raise to ₹1 lakh (was ₹50,000). This covers savings, FD and post office deposits for those 60+. Update any retirement planning documents.
Disability deduction moved to Section 150. ₹75,000 for disability and ₹1.25 lakh for severe disability unchanged.

sections.limit_changed_note: Rebate under new regime: income up to ₹12 lakh fully exempt via ₹60,000 rebate. Salaried: ₹12.75 lakh effective threshold (with ₹75,000 standard deduction).
sections.plain_english_summary: The tax rebate section moved to 156. Major benefit: individuals earning up to ₹12 lakh pay zero tax under new regime (up from ₹7 lakh). Salaried individuals get zero tax up to ₹12.75 lakh. This affects all payroll tax computations.

sections.new_title: Relief when salary paid in arrears or in advance
sections.plain_english_summary: Arrears salary relief moved to Section 157. Form 10E (now renumbered) still required before filing ITR. Computation method unchanged.

The new tax regime (115BAC) is now the default regime under Section 202. Old regime with deductions still available but must be opted into explicitly. Payroll must default to new regime unless employees declare otherwise.
Domestic company 25% tax rate moved to Section 199. Conditions (turnover ≤ ₹400 crore or incorporated after certain dates) unchanged. Read with Section 205 for conditions.
22% corporate tax option (no deductions/exemptions) moved to Section 200. All conditions for eligibility unchanged. Most established companies prefer this route.
15% tax for new manufacturing companies moved to Section 201. Incorporated and commenced production conditions unchanged. Investment deadline extended.
Search and seizure powers moved to Section 247. Same powers for CBDT to authorise searches. No substantive change in scope or procedure.
ITR filing provisions moved to Section 263. July 31 deadline for salaried individuals unchanged. Non-audit professionals now get August 31 deadline (extended from July 31).
Scrutiny assessment provisions moved to Section 280. Faceless assessment scheme continues. Time limits for assessment unchanged.
Reassessment provisions moved to Section 284. 3-year normal limit and 10-year limit for high-value evasion unchanged. Important: old Act still governs reassessments opened before April 1, 2026.
Reassessment notice provisions moved to Section 285. Prior approval requirements and time limits unchanged.
Rectification provisions moved to Section 293. 4-year window from date of order to apply for rectification unchanged. Both taxpayer and department can initiate.

Salary TDS moved to Section 392. Rates unchanged (slab-based). Quarterly return now on Form 138 (replaces Form 24Q). Payroll software and TDS return systems must be updated to new section and form numbers.
Securities interest TDS merged into consolidated Section 393. Rate of 10% and ₹10,000 threshold unchanged. Section 393 houses all non-salary resident TDS — refer to table entry 1.
Dividend TDS merged into Section 393 table. 10% rate and ₹5,000 threshold unchanged. Applicable when a company pays dividends to resident shareholders.

sections.new_title: TDS on interest from banks, FDs, NBFCs
sections.limit_changed_note: Senior citizen threshold raised from ₹50,000 to ₹1,00,000. Others threshold: ₹50,000 for banks; ₹5,000 for others — unchanged.
sections.plain_english_summary: Bank/FD interest TDS merged into Section 393. Senior citizen threshold raised to ₹1 lakh. Banks and NBFCs must update TDS deduction triggers in their systems. Payment code varies by payee type (codes 1020, 1021, 1022).

sections.new_title: TDS on payments for work / contracts
sections.plain_english_summary: Contractor TDS merged into Section 393. Rates unchanged: 1% for individuals/HUF, 2% for others. ₹30,000 per contract and ₹1 lakh annual threshold unchanged. New: manpower supply now explicitly included. All vendor invoices must reference new section.
Insurance commission TDS merged into Section 393. 5% rate and ₹15,000 threshold unchanged.
Commission/brokerage TDS merged into Section 393. 5% rate and ₹15,000 threshold unchanged. Applies to all commission agents, distributors, and brokers.
Rent TDS merged into Section 393. 10% on plant/machinery, 10% on land/building/furniture. ₹50,000 per month threshold unchanged. Landlord PAN now required on HRA claims.

sections.new_title: TDS on rent by individual or HUF
sections.plain_english_summary: Individual/HUF rent TDS (for those not subject to tax audit) merged into Section 393. 5% rate on monthly rent above ₹50,000 unchanged. One-time deduction at lease end or year end.

sections.old_title: TDS on professional or technical fees
sections.new_title: TDS on fees for professional or technical services
sections.plain_english_summary: Professional fees TDS merged into Section 393. 10% for professionals, 2% for technical services. ₹30,000 threshold unchanged. Covers doctors, lawyers, CAs, consultants, engineers, directors.

sections.new_title: TDS on purchase of immovable property
sections.plain_english_summary: Property purchase TDS merged into Section 393. 1% rate on property value ≥ ₹50 lakh unchanged. New: buyers purchasing from NRI sellers can now use PAN instead of TAN for TDS deduction.
Goods purchase TDS merged into Section 393. 0.1% rate on annual purchases above ₹50 lakh from a single seller unchanged. Applies to buyers with annual turnover above ₹10 crore.

sections.new_title: TDS on benefit or perquisite to business
sections.plain_english_summary: Business perquisites TDS (gifts, freebies, travel, hospitality given by businesses) merged into Section 393. 10% rate and ₹20,000 annual threshold unchanged.
Crypto/VDA TDS merged into Section 393. 1% rate and ₹10,000 threshold for specified persons, ₹50,000 for others unchanged. CBDT guidelines are now legally binding on this section.
Non-resident TDS provisions merged into Section 393 under a separate NR table. Rates governed by DTAA or Act, whichever is beneficial. No substantive change in rates.

sections.new_title: TDS on income of foreign institutional investors
sections.plain_english_summary: FII income TDS merged into Section 393 NR table. 20% rate unchanged. Applies to securities income of FIIs/FPIs.

sections.new_title: Certificate for lower or nil deduction
sections.plain_english_summary: Lower TDS certificate process moved to Section 396. Process being automated with predefined eligibility rules. Form 13 equivalent continues. Nil/lower certificate mechanism — which was accidentally dropped from original 2025 Bill — was restored by Select Committee.

sections.new_title: Duty to furnish certificate of tax deduction
sections.plain_english_summary: TDS certificate issuance obligation moved to Section 397. Timelines for issuing Form 16 (now Form 130) and Form 16A (now Form 131) unchanged.

sections.limit_changed_note: TCS on foreign tour packages reduced to flat 2%. TCS on LRS for education/medical also reduced. TCS threshold on LRS remittances raised from ₹7 lakh to ₹10 lakh.
sections.plain_english_summary: All TCS provisions consolidated under Section 394. Flat 2% TCS on overseas tour packages (reduced from 5%/20%). LRS threshold raised to ₹10 lakh. Education/medical remittances TCS reduced. Sellers and operators must update billing systems.

sections.new_title: Higher deduction rate for non-filers of return
sections.plain_english_summary: Double TDS rate for those who haven't filed returns moved to Section 398. Check compliance portal before each payment. Unchanged in operation.
Advance tax obligation moved to Section 404. ₹10,000 annual tax liability threshold unchanged. June/September/December/March installment schedule unchanged.

sections.new_title: Interest for default in filing return
sections.plain_english_summary: Late filing interest moved to Section 411. 1% per month on tax due unchanged. Return deadline extended to March 31 with additional charges beyond December.

sections.old_title: Interest for default in advance tax
sections.new_title: Interest for default in advance tax
sections.plain_english_summary: Advance tax shortfall interest moved to Section 412. 1% per month for shortfall below 90% of assessed tax unchanged.

sections.old_title: Interest for deferment of advance tax
sections.new_title: Interest for deferment of advance tax installments
sections.plain_english_summary: Advance tax installment deferment interest moved to Section 413. 1% per month for shortfall in June/September/December installments unchanged.

sections.new_title: Fee for default in filing return
sections.plain_english_summary: Late filing fee moved to Section 416. ₹5,000 fee for income above ₹5 lakh; ₹1,000 for others. Unchanged. Note: return deadline now extended — late filing window goes to March 31.
Under-reporting penalty moved to Section 433. 50% of tax for under-reporting, 200% for misreporting unchanged.

sections.old_title: Penalty for failure to get accounts audited
sections.new_title: Penalty for failure to get accounts audited
sections.plain_english_summary: Tax audit non-compliance penalty moved to Section 439. 0.5% of sales or ₹1.5 lakh (whichever is lower) unchanged.

sections.new_title: Prosecution for wilful attempt to evade tax
sections.plain_english_summary: Tax evasion prosecution moved to Section 460. Maximum imprisonment reduced from 7 years to 2 years for smaller evasion amounts. Procedural lapses like non-production of books now attract fines only, no prosecution.

Annual information reporting expanded under Section 310. AIS (Annual Information Statement) now covers more transaction types. Data-driven compliance push — ensure all financial transactions are reconcilable.

sections.new_title: Rounding off of total income and tax
sections.plain_english_summary: Rounding off provisions moved to Section 314. Income rounded to nearest ₹10, tax to nearest rupee. Unchanged.
NRI foreign employment income deduction moved to Section 144. Conditions unchanged.

sections.new_title: Exemption on transfer of agricultural land
sections.plain_english_summary: Agricultural land LTCG exemption moved to Section 82. 2-year reinvestment window in agricultural land unchanged.

sections.old_title: Exemption on sale of non-residential assets
sections.new_title: Exemption on transfer of long-term capital asset other than house
sections.plain_english_summary: Section 54F (reinvest any LTCG into a house to save tax) moved to Section 84. Conditions: reinvest net consideration, own only one residential house at transfer time. Unchanged.
Transport operator presumptive taxation moved to Section 63. ₹1,000/day for heavy goods vehicles, ₹7,500/month for others unchanged.
Accounting method provisions moved to Section 276. Mercantile (accrual) or cash basis allowed. ICDS (Income Computation and Disclosure Standards) still applies. No change.

sections.old_title: Tax on dividends, royalties for non-residents
sections.new_title: Tax on dividends, interest, royalties for non-residents
sections.plain_english_summary: Non-resident dividend/royalty flat rate provisions moved to Section 196. Rates of 20% (dividends), 10% (royalties from approved agreements) unchanged. DTAA override continues.

sections.new_title: Deduction for income of co-operative societies
sections.plain_english_summary: Co-operative society income deductions moved to Section 138. Full deduction for agricultural income, ₹50,000 for banking, ₹1 lakh for cottage industries — all unchanged.
R&D expenditure deduction moved to Section 37. In-house R&D weighted deduction rules unchanged. Contributions to DSIR-approved institutions deductible at 100%.

sections.new_title: Exemption for educational and medical institutions
sections.plain_english_summary: University, school, and hospital income exemptions moved to Schedule II. ₹5 crore receipt threshold for mandatory approval unchanged. Trust registration rules apply.

sections.new_title: Income of charitable trusts and institutions
sections.plain_english_summary: Charitable trust income exemption moved to Section 332. 85% application of income requirement unchanged. Trust registration process (Form 10A equivalent) mandatory.
Trust registration provisions moved to Section 334. Re-registration requirement for all trusts that registered before 2021 under old scheme continues.

sections.old_title: Deduction for undertakings in hill states
sections.new_title: Deduction for specified businesses in hill states
sections.plain_english_summary: Hill state business deduction (Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh etc.) moved to Section 135. 100% deduction for first 5 years, 25%/30% thereafter unchanged.

sections.old_title: TDS on income from securitization trusts
sections.new_title: TDS on income from securitization trusts
sections.plain_english_summary: Securitization trust income TDS merged into Section 393. 25% for individuals/HUF, 30% for others, 10% for NR individuals. Unchanged.

sections.old_title: TDS on interest on bonds for FIIs
sections.plain_english_summary: Section 194LD has been removed entirely and is no longer applicable after March 31, 2026. If your system has this section mapped, remove it. Interest on these instruments will be covered by general NR TDS provisions.

sections.new_title: Declaration for nil deduction of tax
sections.plain_english_summary: Forms 15G and 15H are merged into a single Form 121 from April 1, 2026. All banks, NBFCs, and deductors must update their submission processes. Old Form 15G/15H will not be accepted from Tax Year 2026-27.
PAN provisions moved to Section 267. PAN now mandatory for a wider range of transactions. PAN-Aadhaar linking mandatory — failure leads to higher TDS deduction and potential account freezes.

sections.new_title: Deduction for contribution to National Pension System
sections.plain_english_summary: NPS deduction moved to Section 124. Employee contribution up to 10% of salary, employer contribution up to 14% (government employees) / 10% (others) unchanged. Additional ₹50,000 deduction under (1B) also unchanged. NPS withdrawals on/after Aug 29, 2024 are fully tax-free.
Section 10(38) was already removed in 2018. LTCG on listed equity is taxable at 12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh under the new Act. Documents still referencing '10(38) exemption' are outdated by several years.

sections.new_title: Deduction for employment of new workers
sections.plain_english_summary: New employee hiring deduction moved to Section 140. 30% of additional employee costs for 3 years unchanged. Minimum 25 new regular employees, minimum ₹25,000/month salary condition unchanged.
Preliminary expenses amortisation moved to Section 43. 5-year equal amortisation and 5% of capital/project cost cap unchanged.
MAT provisions moved to Section 211. 15% of book profits rate unchanged. MAT credit carryforward for 15 years unchanged. Does not apply to companies opting for Section 200/201 regimes.

sections.new_title: Deduction for employees PF and ESI contributions
sections.plain_english_summary: Employee PF/ESI deductibility rules moved to Section 29(2). Critical: deduction only allowed if paid before due date under PF/ESI laws. Late deposits are still disallowed — this rule is unchanged and frequently audited.

sections.new_title: Disallowance of cash payments above threshold
sections.plain_english_summary: Cash payment disallowance rules moved to Section 40. ₹10,000 per day per person limit (₹35,000 for transport) unchanged. Payments above this in cash are fully disallowed as business expense.

sections.old_title: Certain deductions on actual payment basis
sections.new_title: Deductions allowed only on actual payment
sections.plain_english_summary: 43B deductions (taxes, PF, bonus, interest to financial institutions, MSME payments) moved to Section 44. MSME payment rule (pay within 45 days or disallow) is still active and increasingly enforced.

sections.old_title: Furnishing of information by Indian concern
sections.plain_english_summary: Reporting obligations of Indian entities for international group transactions moved to Section 309. Country-by-country report and master file obligations unchanged.

forms.old_purpose: Annual TDS certificate for salaried employees
forms.new_purpose: Annual certificate of tax deduction on salary
forms.structural_changes: Format retained. New section references throughout. Must be issued by June 15 after the end of Tax Year.

forms.old_purpose: Quarterly TDS certificate for non-salary deductions
forms.structural_changes: Format unchanged. References updated. Issued within 15 days of TDS return due date.

forms.new_purpose: Quarterly return of tax deduction on salary
forms.structural_changes: FVU codes reassigned. Section references updated. Q4 deadline remains May 31. Must reference Tax Year, not AY.

forms.new_purpose: Quarterly return of tax deduction — resident non-salary
forms.structural_changes: All section references updated to new 393 table entries. FVU codes reassigned. Validate with updated FVU tool.

forms.new_purpose: Quarterly return of tax deduction — non-residents
forms.structural_changes: Section references updated. NRI property TDS: buyer can use PAN instead of TAN.

forms.new_purpose: Quarterly return of tax collection at source
forms.structural_changes: Section references updated to 394. TCS rate changes (2% flat on foreign tours, LRS threshold ₹10 lakh) must be reflected.

forms.new_purpose: Certificate of tax collection at source

forms.old_purpose: Declaration by non-senior-citizen for nil TDS
forms.new_purpose: Declaration for nil deduction of tax (unified)
forms.structural_changes: Forms 15G and 15H merged into single Form 121 from April 1, 2026. Old forms NOT accepted. All banks and deductors must update their declaration forms immediately.

forms.old_purpose: Declaration by senior citizen for nil TDS
forms.new_purpose: Declaration for nil deduction of tax (unified)
forms.structural_changes: Merged into Form 121 along with Form 15G. Senior citizen threshold now ₹1 lakh for interest income.

Old Clause 34 (TDS disclosure) now split across Clauses 49, 50, 51 with dedicated schedule. Clause 34(b) now requires exact count of unreported TDS transactions (was Yes/No tick). Significant format change — update audit templates.

forms.old_purpose: Relief claim for salary arrears under Section 89
forms.structural_changes: Must be filed before ITR to claim Section 157 relief. Form number pending final CBDT notification — verify before filing.
Renumbered. All new trust registrations and re-registrations must use the new form once notified.

forms.new_purpose: ITR for salaried individuals with up to 2 house properties
forms.structural_changes: Now allows up to 2 house properties (was 1). References updated to new Act. For income earned from April 1, 2026 onwards under new Act.

forms.old_purpose: ITR for individuals with business/profession income
forms.new_purpose: ITR for individuals/HUF with business or profession income
forms.structural_changes: Extended due date: August 31 (was July 31) for non-audit cases. Section references updated throughout.
Extended due date: August 31 for non-audit. Section references updated. Presumptive limits unchanged.

forms.new_purpose: Application for lower or nil deduction certificate
forms.structural_changes: Process being automated. Predefined eligibility rules apply. Form number pending final notification.
Renumbered. MAT rate and conditions unchanged.
Renumbered. Transfer pricing provisions unchanged substantively.
